phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now in this problem, we are given that
a tour bus covers one hundred fifty kilometer
at a speed of seventy-five kilometer per hour.
Then it halts for thirty minutes.
After that,
it returns the same one hundred and fifty kilometer
at a speed of fifty kilometer per hour.
The question is asking us to find the average speed, including the halt.
So we know the formula,
average speed is equal to total distance divided by total time.
So first,
let us find the total distance.
The bus travels one hundred fifty kilometer
in the onward journey and another one hundred fifty kilometer while returning.
So total distance is equal to one hundred fifty plus one hundred fifty. That gives us three hundred kilometers. Now let us find the total time.
We know time is equal to distance divided by speed.
For the onward journey, time is equal to one hundred fifty
divided by seventy-five.
This gives us two hours. Now let us find the time for the return journey.
Time is equal to one hundred fifty divided by fifty. This gives us three hours.
We are also given that the bus halts for thirty minutes. Thirty minutes means zero point five hour.
Now we have all the time values.
So total time is equal to two
plus three plus zero point five. That gives us five point five hours.
Now we have everything we need.
Average speed is equal to total distance divided by total time.
Putting the values, average speed is equal to three hundred divided by five point five. After simplifying this, we get six hundred by eleven, which is equal to fifty-four and six by eleven kilometer
per hour. So the average speed of the bus, including the halt, is fifty-four and six by eleven kilometer per hour. Hence, the correct answer is option D.
